questions.q: What does it mean for an org to be "source-tracked"?
options: The org charges extra storage fees for metadata
The org can never be deleted once created
The org only allows one developer to connect at a time
The CLI maintains a record of which metadata has changed locally and in the org since the last sync
questions.explain: Source tracking is the CLI maintaining a record of what's changed on both sides (local project and org) since the last sync, which is what lets deploy/retrieve commands act on just the changed set.

questions.q: Why does the very first sf project deploy start to a fresh scratch org deploy the entire project, not just a subset?
options: Because --source-dir is required on the first run
Because every local file is "new" relative to an empty tracking baseline, with nothing yet recorded as already synced
Because scratch orgs ignore source tracking entirely
Because the first deploy always fails and must be retried in full
questions.explain: With no prior sync recorded, every local file looks changed relative to the empty baseline, so the first deploy on a source-tracked org necessarily sends everything; later deploys only send what changed since that point.

questions.q: What is a "conflict" in source tracking terms?
options: The same component changed both locally and in the org since the last sync, with no clear way to know which version should win
A syntax error in an Apex class
Two developers using the same scratch org alias
A scratch org exceeding its duration-days limit
questions.explain: A conflict happens when the same component was changed on both sides — locally and in the org — since the last sync; the CLI reports this rather than silently picking a winner.

questions.q: What does the --ignore-conflicts flag do, and what should you keep in mind before using it?
options: It permanently disables conflict detection for all future operations on that org
It automatically merges both conflicting versions line by line
It forces the deploy or retrieve to proceed despite detected conflicts, which can silently overwrite a change someone else made directly in the org
It only works when --no-track-source was set at org creation
questions.explain: --ignore-conflicts forces the operation through despite conflicts, keeping whichever side you're actively pushing or pulling — a deliberate choice since it can discard the other side's change, such as a teammate's direct org edit.

questions.q: Why would a team deliberately disable source tracking with --no-track-source when creating a scratch org?
options: Source tracking is required and can never actually be disabled
Disabling it is required before any package can be created
It's the only way to enable Dev Hub on that org
In short-lived CI pipelines that deploy once and tear the org down, tracking's query/compare overhead adds time with no real benefit
questions.explain: Source tracking has a real performance cost from querying and comparing state; for CI scratch orgs that exist briefly and get deployed to exactly once, that tracking overhead buys nothing, so --no-track-source skips it.
